title: Pre-Analysis — Potable Water Capacity Increase for Long-Sector ZEPHYR-24 Operations
abstract: Pre-analysis of the larger potable water tank raised for long-sector ZEPHYR-24 operations, covering the belly fairing work it sits on top of and the aft cabin change being scoped in parallel.

sections.objective: Establish whether a larger potable water tank can be installed in the existing bay without moving the distribution line runs or the servicing panel, and what the additional mass does to an aircraft that is already being asked to carry more in the same section. The request came from two operators flying sectors the original capacity was never sized for, and the commercial case is strong; the pre-analysis question is entirely about installation and about what else is arriving in the same area.
sections.findings_summary: Two items were confirmed and both attach to the aft end of the aircraft rather than to the tank itself. The corrosion removal and restoration task on the metallic structure below the bay works the same belly area and is scheduled at an interval that would fall inside the retrofit window for several operators; the tank cradle covers part of the area the task inspects, so either the task is done first or the cradle has to be removable, and removable was not what the design assumed. The second item came from the descriptive text rather than from any identifier: a rear cabin arrangement being scoped in parallel adds monument mass in the same section for the same long-sector reason, and neither dossier had considered the combined loading. Nothing else in the search touched the water and waste installation.
sections.next_steps: Ask the design office whether the tank cradle can be made removable without a mass penalty; if it cannot, add a note requiring the structural restoration task to be completed before the tank is fitted. Send the combined loading case for the tank and the rear cabin arrangement to weight and balance and hold the result in both dossiers. Neither action holds the modification, and the capacity increase itself is accepted as designed.

expected_findings.rationale: The corrosion removal and restoration task inspects the metallic structure that the enlarged tank cradle covers. Its interval falls inside the retrofit window for several operators, and the cradle as designed is not removable.
expected_findings.resolution: Either make the cradle removable or require the restoration task to be completed before the tank is fitted.

evidence.similarity_note: Both add mass to the aft section of a long-sector ZEPHYR-24 for the same operational reason, and both were raised by customer request. The vocabulary is entirely separate — 'potable water capacity increase' against 'rear galley complex and deep stowage arrangement' — and no part number, functional item number, drawing or zone is shared.

expected_findings.rationale: Neither dossier had looked at the other, because one sits in water and waste and the other in furnishings. An aircraft taking both moves further aft than either substantiation assumed.
expected_findings.resolution: Send the combined loading case to weight and balance and hold the result in both dossiers.

type_data.conclusion: Closed with a positive position. The installation is sound; the two findings are a sequencing note against the structural restoration task and a combined loading case shared with the cabin dossier.
